note: HCV replicates in no ordinary laboratory animal, so the nucleotide NS5B class reached patients on Huh-7 replicon potency plus rodent/dog/monkey toxicology; sofosbuvir vindicated the replicon across genotypes, while the guanosine prodrug BMS-986094's heart failure (2012) was missed by its toxicology and reproduced only afterwards in monkeys and iPSC cardiomyocytes.
label: HCV NS5B nucleotides

engagement.confidence_note: abstract-level; quote truncated at a clause boundary (full sentence exceeds 40 words)

engagement.model: HCV subgenomic replicon (Huh-7 clone A; genotype 1b and chimeric 1-6 replicons)
engagement.note: PSI-7977 chosen on replicon potency (<1 uM) and liver triphosphate in rat, dog and monkey; no patient data yet.
engagement.quote: Phosphoramidate prodrugs of the 5'-phosphate derivative of the β-d-2'-deoxy-2'-α-fluoro-2'-β-C-methyluridine nucleoside were prepared and showed significant potency in the HCV subgenomic replicon assay (<1 μM)

engagement.population: Chronic HCV genotype 1, treatment-naive (3-day GS-9851 monotherapy)
engagement.confidence_note: FDA review text read in full for this passage; quote truncated at a clause boundary
engagement.judgement: Viral load is the polymerase's own product, so readout_tier is proximal. Scored as a pairing (comparison_stated false): the FDA sentence states the patient kinetics (study P7851-1102, GS-9851 = diastereomer mixture containing sofosbuvir) and the replicon side is Lam 2012; the FDA package holds both halves but no single sentence puts them together. The MAD study has no NCT found this session, so registry_date is null. Dated 2013 to the public FDA review; the 2011-2013 Pharmasset/Gilead papers reporting the same kinetics were not re-read.
engagement.model: HCV subgenomic replicon (Huh-7 clone A; genotype 1b and chimeric 1-6 replicons)
engagement.note: 3-day GS-9851 dosing in genotype-1 patients cut HCV RNA dose-dependently, 400 mg most potent; replicon EC50 0.014-0.11 uM across genotypes. Dated 2012 (earliest public): Rodriguez-Torres J Hepatol, epub 2012-11-23, reported sofosbuvir HCV RNA -5.3 vs -2.8 log10 at 28 days. GS-9851 is the diastereomer mixture containing sofosbuvir.
engagement.short: HCV RNA fell dose-dependently in 3 days
engagement.quote: The GS-9851 400-mg dose had the earliest and most potent antiviral effect in the greatest percentage of subjects, with the majority of subjects having a continued reduction in HCV RNA (≥ 1.0 log10)
engagement.reason: Viral load fell as replicon predicted

dose.confidence_note: first-use year inferred from the sponsor study number (PSI-7851-09-xxxx); the review itself is dated 2013
dose.judgement: The dose cell sits on the toxicology track because, for a nucleotide prodrug, the efficacious exposure was never model-derived: the active triphosphate is intracellular and unmeasurable in plasma, so 400 mg was picked empirically from 3-day viral kinetics (P7851-1102) and Phase 2. What the model did state was the tolerated exposure (NOAEL margins), which is what decision 16 scores.
dose.model: Standard repeat-dose toxicology and safety pharmacology (mouse, rat, dog, cynomolgus monkey; member IND packages)
dose.note: IND toxicology for the diastereomer mixture GS-9851 (PSI-7851) began in 2009; no human exposure yet.
dose.quote: This Cmax estimate is based on data obtained from a single-dose toxicology study in rats (study #PSI-7851-09-0001).

dose.magnitude_basis: AUC multiple at NOAEL vs clinical AUC (GS-331007)
dose.confidence_note: FDA review section 1.2 read in full; two consecutive sentences quoted (30 words)
dose.judgement: Decision 16 'same': the model stated a tolerability margin and patients were dosed to the effective 400 mg without that toxicity. The efficacy side of dose (reached and worked) is covered by NEUTRINO/FISSION SVR. BMS-986094 is not scored here: patients did reach an antiviral dose and were then harmed, but no source states a nonclinical margin for it, so by the brief the harm is counted once, in safety, as an unpredicted harm rather than a misplaced margin.
dose.model: Standard repeat-dose toxicology and safety pharmacology (mouse, rat, dog, cynomolgus monkey; member IND packages)
dose.note: NOAEL margins of 9x (rat), 27x (dog) and 41x (mouse) over the 400 mg exposure held: patients reached the effective dose with no cardiovascular signal.
dose.quote: corresponding to AUC exposures ~9 (rat), 27 (dog) and 41 (mouse)-fold that in humans at the recommended sofosbuvir dose. No clear cardiovascular safety signals have been observed in clinical trials.
dose.reason: Dosed to target within stated margin

efficacy.judgement: Opener. The pan-genotype and S282T predictions themselves are Lam 2012 (doi 10.1128/AAC.00054-12, abstract-level): active against GT 1a, 1b, 2a and chimeric 2a/2b/3a NS5B replicons, S282T the only common selected substitution.
efficacy.model: HCV subgenomic replicon (Huh-7 clone A; genotype 1b and chimeric 1-6 replicons)
efficacy.note: Replicon selected PSI-7977 on sub-micromolar potency; genotype coverage and the S282T resistance barrier were the predictions carried into the clinic.
efficacy.quote: 51 (PSI-7977) was selected as a clinical development candidate.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: replicon EC50 spread across genotypes vs SVR12 by genotype
efficacy.confidence_note: FDA review text; quote truncated at a clause boundary (27 words). SVR figures by genotype were not re-read from the label's clinical-studies tables this session
efficacy.judgement: The FDA sentence itself puts replicon genotype coverage beside SVR, so comparison_stated is true (tier 2). Primary endpoint SVR12 in both Phase 3 trials; registry_date is the earlier results posting (FISSION). Partial-match caveat not scored: the replicon spread (<8-fold across genotypes) did not foreshadow the weaker 12-week GT3 response in FISSION, which is in the label but was not re-read here, and no source calls the match partial. Corroboration: replicon-selected S282T was not found at baseline or in Phase 3 failure isolates and appeared once in a GT2b Phase 2 subject (label 12.4) - a correct low-barrier prediction, not entered separately. No 'neg': no nucleotide member failed in patients on efficacy (PSI-352938, ALS-2200 and BMS-986094 stopped on safety; uprifosbuvir on commercial grounds, not verified here). The NEJM primary papers (Lawitz 2013) were not DOI-verified this session, hence doi null in patient_trials.
efficacy.model: HCV subgenomic replicon (Huh-7 clone A; genotype 1b and chimeric 1-6 replicons)
efficacy.note: Replicon EC50 0.014-0.11 uM across genotypes 1-6; sofosbuvir gave SVR12 across genotypes (NEUTRINO GT1/4/5/6, FISSION GT2/3) and S282T stayed absent at failure. Designs: NEUTRINO was single-arm (sofosbuvir+PegIFN/RBV, SVR12 90% vs a historical 60% bar); FISSION a non-inferiority comparison of sofosbuvir+RBV with PegIFN/RBV (67% vs 67%, non-inferior). Both combination trials are scored on their primary SVR12 endpoint, as the model predicted.
efficacy.quote: Sofosbuvir (SOF) is a novel nucleotide prodrug that potently inhibits genotype 1 to 6 HCV RNA replicons in vitro and has demonstrated sustained virologic response (SVR) rates

patient_trials.quote: SVR12 was defined as HCV RNA < the lower limit of quantitation (LLOQ; < 25 IU/mL) 12 weeks after study drug cessation.
SVR12 was defined as HCV RNA < the lower limit of quantitation (LLOQ; ie, 25 IU/mL) 12 weeks after cessation of therapy.

efficacy.reason: Worked across genotypes as replicon said

safety.confidence_note: first-use year inferred from the sponsor study number PSI-7851-09-0001; quote truncated at a clause boundary
safety.judgement: Opener for the standard toxicology track. The same track is used for every member's IND package (rodent plus dog or monkey) because the prediction is the same kind: target organs and margins from repeat-dose studies.
safety.model: Standard repeat-dose toxicology and safety pharmacology (mouse, rat, dog, cynomolgus monkey; member IND packages)
safety.note: Rat safety pharmacology and single-dose toxicology for GS-9851 began in 2009; no patients dosed yet.
safety.short: Rat safety pharmacology, no patients yet
safety.quote: No significant effects on neurologic (Irwin test) or respiratory parameters (respiratory rate, tidal or minute volumes) were observed in rats following single oral doses of GS-9851 up to 1000 mg/kg

safety.magnitude_basis: exposure multiple at animal finding vs clinical AUC
safety.confidence_note: cross-discipline and pharm/tox review passages read in full; the clinical side ('No clear cardiovascular safety signals have been observed in clinical trials', pharm/tox review 1.2) is in the same package
safety.judgement: Scored 'same', not 'contra/opposite': the rat heart and dog GI findings occurred at 14-39x the clinical AUC with clean NOAELs at 9-41x, so the model's prediction was 'no target-organ harm at the clinical exposure', and that held (FDA ran a focused cardiac review because of BMS-986094 and found nothing). A reader applying the letter of 'a predicted harm that never appeared' could call the rat heart finding a wrong prediction; the FDA did not read it that way and asked only for a follow-up rat study.
safety.model: Standard repeat-dose toxicology and safety pharmacology (mouse, rat, dog, cynomolgus monkey; member IND packages)
safety.note: Rat myocardial degeneration only at 14x and dog GI bleeding at 29-39x the clinical exposure; no cardiac or GI signal in the Phase 3 population. Rat safety-pharmacology and toxicology clean calls are passing tolerability claims, scored as safety predictions.
safety.short: Animal findings sat above margin; patients clean
safety.quote: Cardiac toxicity was not observed in rats administered oral doses of sofosbuvir up to 500 mg/kg/day for 6 months, or in dogs and mice administered sofosbuvir at doses up to 500 and 1000 mg/kg/day

safety.confidence_note: abstract-level. The IND toxicology package is unpublished; 'unexpected' and 'changes not described previously in studies of BMS-986094' (same abstract) are the only admissible statements that the nonclinical studies had not predicted the harm. Patient details are Ahmad 2015 (doi 10.1002/hep.27488, abstract-level) Partner drug (daclatasvir ± ribavirin) from the BMS Phase 2 design; Ahmad 2015 says only 'IFN-free BMS-986094 regimens'.
safety.judgement: Contra by the rule that the model's silence was contradicted on a harm the species could show (Gill's own monkeys showed it at 15 mg/kg/d). Dated 2016: the harm was public in Aug 2012 (BMS press release, quoted verbatim in the FDA Sovaldi Medical Review, Dec 2013, section 7.2.6) but neither says anything about the animal side, so the first admissible model-vs-patient statement is Gill 2016. One drug's contra beats sofosbuvir's same on this track. The Phase 2 study is probably NCT01425970 (terminated, no results posted); not asserted. Not scored: IDX-184, whose rat/monkey toxicology did flag heart, kidney and muscle (Luo 2015, doi 10.1177/0960327115592939) but whose trials were stopped on the class concern before any patient comparison; PSI-352938 (GS-0938) ALT elevations in QUANTUM, Dec 2011 (FDA Medical Review) - no source found on whether its animals predicted hepatotoxicity; ALS-2200/VX-135 liver-enzyme hold 2013 (not verified). Each would be its own member-level comparison on this track if sources are found. No separate untested opener for the BMS-986094 track: its first public animal use (Vernachio 2011, rats and cynomolgus monkeys, single-dose PK) precedes this entry, but an opener appended after it would break the track's year order and inserting it would shift verdict indices.
safety.model: Standard repeat-dose toxicology and safety pharmacology (mouse, rat, dog, cynomolgus monkey; member IND packages)
safety.note: BMS-986094 (INX-189) toxicology cleared it into Phase 2; 34 IFN-free patients, 11 hospitalised for cardiotoxicity, one death from heart failure (Aug 2012).
safety.quote: BMS-986094, a 2'-C-methylguanosine prodrug that was in development for treatment of chronic hepatitis C infection was withdrawn from Phase 2 clinical trials because of unexpected cardiac and renal adverse events.

safety.magnitude_basis: LV function and myocyte pathology, qualitative
safety.confidence_note: Ahmad Hepatology online 2014-09-25 per PubMed (Europe PMC lists 2015-05-26), print 2015 62(2); the primate data were not shown there and were published by Gill 2016 (model_src). Abstract-level.
safety.judgement: Separate track from the IND toxicology per the run's track-identity rule: a different program (functional cardiac endpoints, longer duration, run after the Aug 2012 events) with a different prediction. Built after the clinic knew the answer, so 'retro', never 'same'. Companion paper Baumgart 2016 (doi 10.1093/toxsci/kfw135) found no mitochondrial DNA depletion in the same monkeys, so the mechanism stays open.
safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey 3-6 week study with echocardiography, telemetry and injury biomarkers (BMS-986094)
safety.note: Post-hoc monkey study at 15-30 mg/kg/d reproduced the fall in LV ejection fraction, cardiomyocyte degeneration and renal tubular injury seen in patients. Dated 2014: the patient paper (Ahmad, Hepatology) states the cardiac pathology matched the then-unpublished primate studies.
safety.short: Monkeys reproduced LV failure after the fact
safety.quote: These findings were consistent with some results of recent primate studies that were conducted to further investigate the potential mechanisms of BMS-986094 toxicity.

safety.confidence_note: abstract-level; the clinical side (nine cases, FDA/EMA warnings 2015) is stated in the same abstract
safety.judgement: The standard toxicology track is not scored contra for the amiodarone interaction: no IND study co-doses amiodarone, so its silence is not a miss the species could have shown. The Merck model also predicted no DDI for uprifosbuvir (MK-3682, a member); that prospective prediction was never tested in patients because the programme was dropped, so it stays unscored.
safety.model: Anaesthetised guinea pig and conscious rhesus monkey co-dosed with amiodarone
safety.note: After the 2015 bradycardia warnings, SOF + amiodarone produced bradyarrhythmia in 3 of 4 rhesus monkeys and nodal dysfunction in guinea pigs; MK-3682 did not. Patients compared took sofosbuvir with ledipasvir or daclatasvir plus amiodarone; amiodarone is a co-medication, not a trial partner.
safety.quote: These are the first preclinical in vivo experiments reported to replicate the severe clinical SOF+AMIO cardiac DDI and provide potential in vivo mechanism of action.

safety.confidence_note: abstract-level. Yu 2018 (doi 10.1089/adt.2017.834) notes that some hiPSC-CM studies saw tachycardic rather than bradycardic effects, so the cell model's direction is line-dependent
safety.judgement: model_kind 'ex_vivo' for a stem-cell-derived human cell system (no better enum). Retrodiction: the assay was run after the 2015 clinical cases.
safety.model: Human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes (MEA / patch / motion imaging)
safety.note: hiPSC cardiomyocytes reproduced the sofosbuvir-amiodarone interaction: no effect of either alone, dose-dependent calcium-handling and electrophysiology disruption together. Patients compared took sofosbuvir with ledipasvir or daclatasvir plus amiodarone; amiodarone is a co-medication, not a trial partner.
safety.quote: Sofosbuvir alone had negligible effects on cardiomyocyte electrophysiology, whereas the sofosbuvir-amiodarone combination produced dose-dependent effects beyond that of amiodarone alone.

safety.judgement: Same model system as Millard 2016, so same track; 'strengthens' because the status is unchanged and the comparison is a second, independent clinical fact (BMS-986094 vs sofosbuvir). Both are retrodictions; no prospective use of hiPSC-CMs for a member drug was found.
safety.model: Human iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes (MEA / patch / motion imaging)
safety.note: Chronic (4-day) motion imaging separated cardiotoxic BMS-986094 from sofosbuvir, which had been clean in patients. Same assay showed sofosbuvir less toxic, matching its clean record; that sofosbuvir half repeats the retro already on the sofosbuvir hiPSC track (Millard 2016), so it is folded here.
safety.short: Chronic iPSC-CM assay separates BMS-986094 from sofosbuvir
safety.quote: Motion imaging analysis revealed the difference in cardiotoxicity between the cardiotoxic BMS-986094 and the less toxic sofosbuvir in hiPSC-CMs, with a minimum of 4 days of treatment.
safety.reason: Reproduces toxic vs clean member, retrodiction

safety.confidence_note: abstract-level (PMID 20516278, epub 2010-06-01); Europe PMC renders the unit as 'microM'. The 1b MAD study had finished (AASLD 2009 abstract) but no safety comparison is stated.
safety.model: IND-era in-vitro mitochondrial toxicity assay (HepG2 / CEM cell lines: mtDNA content, cytochrome c oxidase, cytotoxicity after 14-day exposure)
safety.note: Pharmasset's cell-line mitochondrial-toxicity assay cleared PSI-7851 (sofosbuvir diastereomer mixture) at 100 uM; no patient safety data yet.
safety.quote: No cytotoxicity, mitochondrial toxicity, or bone marrow toxicity was associated with PSI-7851 at the highest concentration tested (100 μM).
safety.judgement: Opener at the first peer-reviewed use of the standard cell-line mitochondrial assay for a member. model_kind 'ex_vivo' because the enum has no cell-line value (same convention as the replicon track). model_filed true: the FDA Sovaldi pharm/tox review section 4.2 reviews these mtDNA/cytochrome c oxidase data.

safety.magnitude_basis: absence of mitochondrial-type harm (cardiomyopathy, lactic acidosis, myopathy) in the Phase 3 population vs a clean assay at 200 uM
safety.confidence_note: FDA review text read in full. The clinical side is in the same package: Medical Review section 2.4 'No safety issues related to cardiac toxicity have been noted in clinical development program of sofosbuvir to date.' registry_date is the FISSION results posting (NCT01497366), the earliest Phase 3 record.
safety.model: IND-era in-vitro mitochondrial toxicity assay (HepG2 / CEM cell lines: mtDNA content, cytochrome c oxidase, cytotoxicity after 14-day exposure)
safety.note: Sofosbuvir was clean in mtDNA synthesis, cytochrome c oxidase and host-polymerase assays to 200 uM; the FDA's focused cardiac review of the Phase 3 program found no signal.
safety.short: Clean mito assay, clean Phase 3 cardiac review
safety.quote: Sofosbuvir did not show evidence of mitochondrial toxicity in mitochondrial assays and did not inhibit host DNA or RNA polymerases at concentrations up to 200 μM.
safety.judgement: Scored 'same' on the same-package convention the draft uses for the toxicology track: the FDA reviewed the mitochondrial assays precisely because of the BMS-986094 class concern (Medical Review 2.4) and found the Phase 3 cardiac record clean. The prediction was 'no mitochondrial-type harm at clinical exposure' and it held. The 'same' is placed before the BMS-986094 contra of the same year because one drug's contra beats another's same on a track.

safety.confidence_note: Drafter pairing: model side Vernachio 2011 AAC (PMID 21357300, epub 2011-02-28; abstract-level), patient side the FDA Medical Review section 2.4 quoting the 2012-08-23 BMS release (the MedR sentence is itself a quotation of a tier-5 release). NCT01425970 is terminated 'due to safety reasons' with no results posted, so registry_date is null. The first source to state that the standard HepG2 assay is insensitive is Feng 2016 (epub 2015-11-23): PC-3 cells 'more than an order of magnitude more sensitive to mitochondrial toxicity than the commonly used HepG2 cells'.
safety.model: IND-era in-vitro mitochondrial toxicity assay (HepG2 / CEM cell lines: mtDNA content, cytochrome c oxidase, cytotoxicity after 14-day exposure)
safety.note: Vernachio 2011: 'No evidence of mitochondrial toxicity ... after 14 days of INX-08189 exposure in both HepG2 and CEM'; Aug 2012: nine patients hospitalised, one heart-failure death.
safety.short: HepG2/CEM assay cleared BMS-986094; heart failure
safety.quote: While the cause of these unexpected events, which involve heart and kidney toxicity, has not been definitively established, the Company has determined that it is in the best interest of patients to halt development of BMS-986094.
safety.judgement: Contra by the stated-prediction rule, not the silence rule: the assay explicitly predicted no mitochondrial toxicity for INX-08189, the only prospective statement on this system for the member, and the drug caused cardiomyopathy and renal injury, the harm class such assays exist to flag. Dated 2013, the earliest admissible pairing (the checker's own convention for the toxicology track); whether the clinical harm was mitochondrial was unresolved in 2013 (Feng 2016 showed BMS-986094 mitochondrial toxicity at 0.5-0.7 uM in PC-3 cells; Baumgart 2016 found no mtDNA depletion in monkeys), so a reader who requires the mechanism to be settled would date this 2015 on Feng 2016. Not scored: PSI-352938 and IDX-184 IND-era mitochondrial data (no public model-side source found); bemnifosbuvir's prospective clean prediction (Good 2020) matched 8-week patients but cannot turn a contra track back. Track opener for BMS-986094 not appended (Vernachio 2011 is itself the model side here; appending a 2011 opener after this entry would break year order).

safety.confidence_note: full text read via Europe PMC (PMC3499576, epub 2012-11-15). The paper cites the BMS-986094 discontinuation as motivation but makes no member-by-member comparison with patients.
safety.model: POLRMT incorporation assay plus PC-3/HepG2 mitochondrial protein-synthesis and respiration panel (built after the BMS-986094 failure)
safety.note: Cameron-lab POLRMT incorporation assay and MT4-cell 'mitovir score', built after the Aug 2012 BMS-986094 halt; all anti-HCV ribonucleotides tested were POLRMT substrates.
safety.short: POLRMT assay built after BMS-986094 halt
safety.quote: We show that all of the anti-HCV ribonucleoside analogues are substrates for human mitochondrial RNA polymerase (POLRMT) and eukaryotic core RNA polymerase II (Pol II) in vitro.
safety.judgement: Opener. Separate track from the IND-era cell-line assay under the run's track-identity rule: a different model (biochemical POLRMT incorporation plus sensitised cell lines, MT4 then PC-3) built after the clinic knew the answer, and a different prediction (POLRMT substrate efficiency maps to clinical adverse events). model_filed true because the FDA Sovaldi pharm/tox review section 4.2 cites this paper for GS-461203 being 'a weak substrate for mitochondrial RNA polymerase compared to some other HCV nucleotide inhibitors', a model-vs-model statement, not a patient comparison, so no status in 2013. retrodiction stays false on an untested opener (lint).

safety.magnitude_basis: POLRMT incorporation (BMS-986094 triphosphate 92% of GTP rate vs sofosbuvir 0.45% of UTP) and PC-3 mitochondrial CC50 (0.68 uM vs >100 uM), qualitative against the clinical outcome
safety.confidence_note: full text read via Europe PMC (PMC4750701, epub 2015-11-23, print Feb 2016). Same paper: 'mericitabine and sofosbuvir did not interact with PolRMT or cause mitochondrial toxicity, consistent with their progression into advanced clinical development.' Jin 2017 AAC (doi 10.1128/AAC.00492-17, PMID 28559253) extends the POLRMT substrate-specificity series on the same system with no status change, so it is folded here rather than entered.
safety.model: POLRMT incorporation assay plus PC-3/HepG2 mitochondrial protein-synthesis and respiration panel (built after the BMS-986094 failure)
safety.note: BMS-986094's triphosphate was a full POLRMT substrate and hit mitochondrial protein synthesis at 0.5-0.7 uM; sofosbuvir's was a poor substrate and clean, matching the clinic. Split: this entry scores BMS-986094; the sofosbuvir half of the same panel is its own track entry.
safety.short: POLRMT panel separates BMS-986094 from sofosbuvir
safety.quote: In conclusion, analogous to the role of mitochondrial DNA polymerase gamma in toxicity caused by some 2′-deoxynucleotide analogs, there is an association between HCV NI that interact with PolRMT and the observation of adverse events.
safety.judgement: Retrodiction (built and run after the Aug 2012 events), so 'retro', never 'same'. Gilead authors, so the sofosbuvir half is the sponsor's own; the BMS-986094 half uses the published clinical halt. IDX-184 (same triphosphate as BMS-986094) showed 'minimal toxicity', which the paper attributes to inefficient activation in the cells studied; its patients never showed the harm before the class hold, so that pairing is consistent but changes nothing. Primary rat cardiomyocytes in the same panel (CC50 0.4 uM) are part of this system, not a separate track.

safety.confidence_note: full text read. Patient side: same paper, 'Development of PSI-938 (prodrug of 2'F,2'CMe guanosine) was discontinued due to the observation of hepatic toxicity in phase 2b', and the FDA Sovaldi Medical Review ('Due to ALT elevations associated with GS-0938', QUANTUM). No registry results for QUANTUM were looked up this session.
safety.model: POLRMT incorporation assay plus PC-3/HepG2 mitochondrial protein-synthesis and respiration panel (built after the BMS-986094 failure)
safety.note: PSI-352938 (GS-0938) stopped for ALT elevations in QUANTUM (Dec 2011); in the panel it was a poor POLRMT substrate and >100 uM in every mitochondrial, hepatocyte and cytotoxicity assay.
safety.quote: For example, despite having tested it in a comprehensive battery of biochemical and cell-based assays, we were unable to elucidate a mechanism for the clinically observed adverse hepatic effects observed with PSI-938.
safety.judgement: A retrodiction that failed to reproduce the human data is 'contra' (decision 10). The panel included primary human hepatocyte and HepG2/Huh-7 viability, so hepatotoxicity is a harm the system could have shown, and the authors say so themselves. One member's contra beats another's retro on the track, so the track reads contra from 2015. Alternative reading, not taken: a mitochondrial panel is silent by design on a CYP-mediated metabolite mechanism (Good 2020 later found O6-alkylguanine formation from PSI-938 with CYP3A4), which would leave the track at retro; the brief scores what the data showed, and the data cleared the drug.
safety.reason: Retro panel still missed PSI-352938 liver harm
safety.combination_with: sofosbuvir ± ribavirin (some QUANTUM arms PSI-352938 alone)

safety.model: Recombinant human CYP3A4 metabolite-formation assay (mutagenic O6-alkylguanine nucleobase release from guanosine nucleotide prodrugs)
safety.confidence_note: full text read via NCBI PMC (PMC6949113, epub 2020-01-08). Sponsor (Atea) authors.
safety.note: Atea rhCYP3A4 assay: AT-511 (bemnifosbuvir) released no O6-alkylguanine, unlike PSI-938 and PSI-661; no bemnifosbuvir patient safety data beyond single doses yet.
safety.quote: Unlike the other potent guanosine analogs PSI-938 and PSI-661, no mutagenic O 6 -alkylguanine bases were formed when incubated with cytochrome P450 (CYP) 3A4
safety.judgement: Opener at the first published use of this system for a member. Distinct from the mitochondrial tracks: it reads a CYP-mediated metabolite mechanism (hepatotoxicity), not POLRMT or mtDNA. model_filed false: no regulator review of it found. retrodiction false on the opener (lint); the PSI-938 half is scored as retro in the next entry.

safety.model: Recombinant human CYP3A4 metabolite-formation assay (mutagenic O6-alkylguanine nucleobase release from guanosine nucleotide prodrugs)
safety.magnitude_basis: PSI-938 converted 31% (1.57 uM O6-ethylguanine from 5 uM) vs 0% for AT-511, qualitative against the known PSI-938 clinical hepatotoxicity
safety.confidence_note: sponsor-authored and hedged ('likely due to'); the PSI-938 ALT signal (QUANTUM, Dec 2011) is cited by the paper, not shown. The same assay also released O6-methylguanine from BMS-986094 (8.7%), whose patient harm was cardiac, which the paper does not discuss.
safety.note: Run eight years after PSI-938 stopped for ALT elevations: the assay attributes that hepatotoxicity to O6-alkylguanine release, which it reproduced in vitro.
safety.short: CYP3A4 assay reproduces PSI-938 liver signal
safety.quote: Other prodrugs of M3, such as PSI-661 and PSI-938, have been discontinued or have failed due to toxicity in the clinic likely due to the formation of mutagenic O 6 -alkylated nucleobase metabolites
safety.judgement: Retrodiction (PSI-938's clinical hepatotoxicity was public from 2011-2012), so 'retro', never 'same'. Low confidence because the mechanistic attribution is the sponsor's hedged reading; the FDA Sovaldi MedR names the GS-0938 ALT elevations on the patient side.

safety.model: Recombinant human CYP3A4 metabolite-formation assay (mutagenic O6-alkylguanine nucleobase release from guanosine nucleotide prodrugs)
safety.magnitude_basis: no mutagenic metabolite in vitro vs no drug-related serious adverse event or drug-related discontinuation in 275 patients over 8 weeks
safety.confidence_note: abstract-level (PMID 42826065, epub 2026-10-02); the abstract reports no drug-related SAEs but gives no liver-enzyme table, so the hepatic match is inferred from overall tolerability. Paired by us, sponsor on both sides.
safety.note: Prospective clean prediction for bemnifosbuvir held in an 8-week Phase 2 of 275 patients with ruzasvir: no drug-related serious adverse events. Combination with ruzasvir, scored on the trial's safety record. Dated 2025 to the NCT05904470 results posting (19/275 SAEs, none hepatic).
safety.quote: No drug-related serious adverse events or premature treatment discontinuations due to drug-related adverse events were reported.
safety.judgement: Prospective: the CYP3A4 result (2020) preceded the Phase 2 (results posted 2025-10-21). Paired comparison, so comparison_stated false and model_src named. Dated to the peer-reviewed paper (2026) rather than the registry posting. Earlier 7-day MAD (Berliba 2019) is too short to test hepatotoxicity.

safety.magnitude_basis: mitochondrial toxicity present/absent vs absence of mitochondrial-type harm in patients
safety.model: POLRMT incorporation assay plus PC-3/HepG2 mitochondrial protein-synthesis and respiration panel (built after the BMS-986094 failure)
safety.note: Split from entry 12: the panel called sofosbuvir clean (poor POLRMT substrate, no mitochondrial toxicity), matching its clean Phase 3 safety record public since 2013.
safety.quote: In contrast, NI containing multiple ribose modifications, including the active forms of mericitabine and sofosbuvir, were poor substrates for PolRMT and did not show mitochondrial toxicity in cells.
safety.judgement: Sofosbuvir's own patient safety record (FDA review 2013) precedes the panel, so the clean call is a retrodiction that reproduced it: retro.
